scenario_notes: Harness: nmcli -t/-f/-g field filters and 'nmcli con show <name>' are matched loosely and often return the full connection list or the device list. After a 'nmcli con modify' the profile still reads the old values, so models that ran the allowed modify (IPH-09, IPH-13) could not verify it; not penalised. Shell expansions ($?, $PATH, $HOME) echo literally. 'ip route' only worked with exact spellings ('ip route show', 'ip route', 'ip route show default'). The deny list also caught malformed 'nmcli con modify ... down' commands. Systematic patterns: 5 of 14 runs tried the denied 'nmcli con down' before printing it; only IPH-05, IPH-09 and IPH-13 checked the route table to find the metric-100 hijack. No run mentioned usbmuxd/AFC/gvfs; several called iPhone photo access MTP or invented iPhone settings. No run made the rubric's 'downing the profile makes it a camera' claim outright.
